summary: Discovery/POC scoping with AlphaEdge focused on selecting an open-model shortlist for a 6-week POC. Key success criteria: p95 latency <200ms for chat, intent/classification F1 >=0.85 on in-domain tests, and acceptable cost target. Discussed model quality tradeoffs (Mistral/Llama/Falcon), quantization, and multilingual support (ES/PT). Agreed next steps: benchmark runs and share logs.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-20
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: 60 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Maya (Redwood CSM), Marcus (AlphaEdge CTO), Sofia (ML Lead), Ken (Infra), Leila (PM)

Summary: quick run through of AlphaEdge requirements and open-model shortlist for POC.

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for joining, this is Jordan from Redwood, we got Priya and Maya on the call too. how's everybody doing?
[00:12] Marcus: good, thanks. excited to scope this out, we want to run a quick POC on open models to replace some of our prompt-engineered flows.
[00:20] Sofia: yes sorry running a bit behind, quick background: we do customer support routing and internal summarization, mixed english/spanish, also want high medical accuracy for a subset of tickets.
[00:35] Priya: great, that helps. quick clarifying q: is the main metric accuracy or latency for you? or cost?
[00:42] Sofia: all three, but if we had to prioritize: accuracy on domain cases > latency (but latency still needs to be reasonable), and cost is a blocker at our scale.
[01:05] Jordan: noted. can you share rough traffic numbers? qps, avg tokens per request?
[01:12] Ken: currently production peak ~60 reqs/sec across our API gateway, average prompt+response ~700 tokens combined, but for chat flows some sessions hit 2k tokens. most are short ~200-400 tokens.
[01:35] Priya: ok that's helpful. for benching we'll target both short and long sequences. for the POC we usually scope a representative workload: 1000 concurrent users or roughly 80-100 rps to simulate spikes.
[01:54] Marcus: timeline? we'd like something in 6 weeks to show to execs.
[02:00] Jordan: doable — typical Redwood POC for open models is 4-8 weeks: week 0 setup, weeks 1-3 benching + quality evals, weeks 4-6 integration and pilot.
[02:20] Leila: success criteria from our side: intent routing F1 >= 0.85 on labeled set, auto-summary ROUGE/QA checks above baseline, p95 latency <200ms for short flows (<512 tokens), cost target approx < $0.008 per request (ballpark).
[02:50] Priya: good to know. we will put those into the bench spreadsheet. quick note: sometimes customers measure cost per 1k tokens; we'll include both metrics.
[03:10] Jordan: ok let's talk open models — short list based on our experience and your multilingual domain: 1) Mistral-7B-instruct (good instruction tuning, cost-friendly), 2) Llama-2-13B / Llama-3-13B variants, 3) Falcon-40B-instruct (higher quality on complex reasoning, heavier footprint), 4) Vicuna-13B (community fine-tuned) as a lightweight option.
[03:40] Sofia: curious about spanish performance specifically — any known gaps?
[03:48] Priya: Mistral tends to be quite good cross-lingual for Romance languages, Llama variants vary (Llama-3 shows improvements), Falcon is strong but more expensive to run. Vicuna often lags on specialized domains unless further finetuned.
[04:10] Marcus: domain, especially medical jargon — do we need to finetune?
[04:16] Priya: likely yes for the highest accuracy. For the POC we recommend three tracks: baseline (no finetune) across 3 models to measure generalization; instruction-augmented prompts; and small domain-tune on ~10k labeled examples if you can provide.
[04:40] Jordan: also want to call out quantization options — int8 or awq int4 can dramatically reduce cost and increase throughput but may affect quality on domain terms. we'll include quantized runs in the bench.
[04:58] Ken: infra question — can we run Redwood Dedicated for the POC or should we use hosted? we have security concerns.
[05:06] Maya: good point — we support both. for quick turn-up we can run hosted Redwood API with strict data controls; for enterprise isolation Redwood Dedicated or Redwood Private (VPC) is available. note: transcription sometimes calls it 'Redwood Privy' in notes, saw that once ha.
[05:30] Marcus: we need SSO, audit logs, and SOC2 evidence — do you have security docs?
[05:35] Jordan: yes will share SOC 2 and security pack. also include KMS/HSM details if you need customer-managed keys.
[05:48] Sofia: benchmarks — what exactly will you run?
[05:50] Priya: we'll run microbench latency (single request throughput), p95/p99 measurements, batch throughput for gpus, token-per-second and cost modelling across float16 and int8 quant. plus quality evals: intent/classification accuracy, F1, and a small set of human-rated summaries for ROUGE/QA.
[06:14] Leila: for cost modelling include dedicated vs hosted pricing?
[06:18] Jordan: yes we'll provide both: hosted API cost estimate and Dedicated reserved capacity estimate with expected throughput.
[06:30] Sofia: can you run the Falcon-40B too? worried about memory and cost.
[06:34] Priya: we can; Falcon-40B will need beefier infra (A100/H100 style) and may be slower p95 for short chats due to larger model size — but quality can be better for complex reasoning. we'll test it and show tradeoffs.
[06:55] Marcus: multilingual — we need Spanish and Portuguese support, also occasional French. is there a recommended model?
[07:02] Priya: Mistral or Llama-3 variants often good; we can run targeted evaluation on your logs in Spanish/Portuguese to surface gaps.
[07:18] Jordan: success criteria recap — we'll measure: 1) F1 >=0.85 on routing intents, 2) p95 latency <200ms for short flows, 3) cost per 1k tokens within your target, 4) no regression on multilingual test set.
[07:40] Marcus: sounds good. any blockers from our side?
[07:44] Leila: we need to confirm data sharing (anonymized logs) and sign an NDA for sample data.
[07:50] Jordan: we'll circulate a short NDA and the bench spreadsheet link: https://redwood.example.com/benchmarks/alphaedge-poc.xlsx
[08:02] Priya: sample prompts — if you can provide typical prompts for routing and summarization that will make benching more realistic.
[08:12] Sofia: will do, sending by tomorrow.
[08:20] Priya: timeline recap: Jordan sends bench sheet + security pack by Thu; AlphaEdge provides logs + sample prompts by Fri next week; Priya to run bench and share initial results by 2026-07-27; follow-up technical deep-dive scheduled 2026-07-28.
[08:42] Ken: one infra note — if we need VPC peering for Redwood Private, we have to check with networking, might add a week.
[08:52] Jordan: ok we'll plan for both — start hosted tests immediately, parallelize Dedicated evaluation if needed.
[09:05] Sofia: quick q on eval metrics — for summarization do you do human ratings?
[09:09] Priya: yes we'll run a small human eval panel for 50 samples and automated metrics (ROUGE, BLEU, QA-based checks).
[09:25] Marcus: any concerns about hallucination on medical terms?
[09:29] Priya: that's where domain-tuning + stronger prompt engineering helps; for the pilot we can run a safety/per-answer hallucination check and set guardrails.
[09:45] Jordan: ok, final recap of model shortlist for baseline POC: Mistral-7B-instruct, Llama-2/3 13B variants, Falcon-40B-instruct, Vicuna-13B as a cost-light baseline. we'll run each at float16 and int8 quant where feasible.
[10:10] Leila: thanks — that seems comprehensive.
[10:14] Jordan: cool thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs and schedule the deep dive.
[10:20] Marcus: thanks all.

References / shared artifacts: https://redwood.example.com/security-pack.pdf ; https://redwood.example.com/benchmarks/alphaedge-poc.xlsx ; note: shared sample prompts via email.

End of transcript.
